incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an extensive AI-powered scam operation. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using artificial intelligence to impersonate him, deceiving vulnerable immigrants into paying thousands of dollars for immigration services he never offered. The fraudulent scheme escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers offering services like US residency assistance for $2,200 cash payments through fake videos and testimonials.

After discovering the fraud when potential clients began calling his office, Leal hired an online anti-piracy company that successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to contact numbers via WhatsApp and send phony contracts. Leal warned consumers to be cautious of requests for payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and emphasized his office never requests payments over the phone. He plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scam's origins.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A fake online article featuring Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock in a heated interview with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler was used to promote Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The fabricated interview never occurred but was designed to appear credible through AI-generated content. This scam represents a growing trend that the Australian Securities and Investments Commission has flagged as increasingly sophisticated and prevalent.

ASIC's recent research shows investment scams jumped significantly, with the regulator removing 19,400 scams last year, a 182 percent increase. The watchdog took down 7,051 fake investment platforms and 5,476 phishing scams. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, politician Pauline Hanson, billionaire Gina Rinehart, and presenter Alan Kohler are among the most commonly impersonated Australians. ASIC warns consumers to verify Australian Financial Services licence numbers and check official registers before investing, though Kohler argues platforms carrying such content should face heavy fines.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A class-action lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco alleges that Oura, a smart ring company valued at $11 billion, made false claims about its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit contends that Oura's rings, which sell for $300 and up, cannot accurately measure sleep stages as advertised and instead rely on unreliable artificial intelligence that is no better than guessing. The lawsuit points out that Oura markets 95 percent accuracy compared to clinical sleep labs, yet lacks the complex equipment those labs use to measure brain activity.

Oura disputes these allegations, stating it stands behind its science and peer-reviewed research validating its sleep staging accuracy. The company explains that its rings estimate sleep stages using multiple physiological signals rather than serving as medical devices. The lawsuit seeks class action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear whether ring purchasers can join the case or what compensation might result. This marks another legal challenge for Oura, which faces a separate ongoing lawsuit over allegedly collecting customer data without consent.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified Aurora ransomware group operations targeting ESXi environments since April 2026. The group deployed a Linux ransomware variant called encrypt.out that encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption and RSA-4096 key wrapping. The ransomware includes an ESXi mode that kills running virtual machines to release file locks, then encrypts VM files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. A custom tool called esxi_finder.py scans networks to locate ESXi hosts and vCenter servers by checking ports 443 and 902 and analyzing TLS certificates.

Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten target organizations across multiple countries. The agent assisted with tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domains, and attempting credential theft attacks. A second cluster of Aurora activity was identified using different methods like SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration, affecting eight victim organizations across six countries. The investigation exposed infrastructure and indicators of compromise to help organizations defend against these threats.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the northeastern United States, filed a lawsuit on May 6 in Texas Business Court. The franchisee claims that Pizza Hut's mandatory rollout of Dragontail, an AI-powered delivery management platform, caused operational problems and customer dissatisfaction. The system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, allowing them to see order timing and tip amounts, which allegedly caused drivers to wait up to fifteen minutes to batch multiple orders together. This resulted in longer delivery times and a significant decline in customer satisfaction and sales.

Before Dragontail launched in 2024, Chaac reported that over 90 percent of pizza deliveries arrived within 30 minutes and the company achieved double-digit sales growth. After implementation, delivery performance deteriorated sharply, with New York City sales swinging from positive 10.19 percent to negative 9.78 percent year-over-year. Chaac alleges the system caused cascading failures and seeks over 100 million dollars in damages plus attorneys' fees. Pizza Hut stated it is reviewing the lawsuit claims and will respond through appropriate legal channels but provided no further comment.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers have been sending fraudulent emails impersonating Terry Gross and other staff members from WHYY's "Fresh Air" program to authors, entertainers and public figures. The personalized messages reference the recipient's work and propose interview topics, creating a convincing booking process. Eventually, the scammers request payment, typically $250, for supposed production costs. Historian Jennifer Black received such an email and initially became excited before noticing red flags like the request coming directly from Gross herself and suspicious AI-generated language. She called WHYY to verify and confirmed it was a scam.

Similar fraudulent emails have been sent impersonating other celebrities including comedians Nikki Glaser and Amy Poehler and journalist Katie Couric. Cybersecurity expert Aunshul Rege explains that artificial intelligence has made impersonation scams more convincing and personalized than traditional mass fraud attempts. WHYY and NPR are investigating with law enforcement and have clarified they never charge guests for interviews. Rege advises recipients to watch for red flags like payment requests and to verify invitations through legitimate contact information rather than responding to suspicious messages.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
A fake American think tank funded by Israel published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots into making pro-Israel arguments. The Hanover Institute, which does not legally exist, presented one-sided content on topics including Palestinian torture, Israeli war crimes, and Gaza starvation as neutral research. The site was built on a platform optimized for search engine results and AI training data, with headlines phrased as chatbot questions. According to filings with the U.S. Justice Department, the operation involved Israeli government funding routed through European advertising company Havas Media and American firms including Piro Inc.

The broader propaganda campaign cost tens of millions of dollars and involved multiple websites seeding AI training databases. Israeli officials have expressed frustration with these efforts, stating the spending failed to improve Israel's public image. American public opinion has shifted significantly against Israel, with polling showing only 36 percent of Americans sympathize with Israel compared to Palestinians. Researchers warn that such AI manipulation represents a growing threat, as poisoned training data influences chatbot responses without requiring users to visit source sites or fact-check information.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records have filed separate lawsuits against Udio and Suno, two popular AI music generators. The labels accuse both companies of scraping copyrighted music without permission and directly reproducing sections of famous songs in their generated outputs. The record labels claim the companies have been deliberately hiding what music they used to train their models, though both previously claimed this constitutes fair use. The lawsuits include a massive list of thousands of copyrighted works allegedly scraped for training, featuring artists like The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Bruce Springsteen, Michael Jackson, and many others.

To support their case, the record labels demonstrated they could repeatedly generate AI songs that closely replicate famous copyrighted tracks by using specific prompts describing the song's era, genre, and artist. For example, prompting for "1954 rock and roll billy haley comets" produced outputs mimicking Bill Haley's style, and a prompt for Mariah Carey produced a near-identical clone of "All I Want for Christmas Is You." The lawsuits, filed in New York and Massachusetts, include a thumb drive of problematic AI-generated music as evidence and represent a major legal battle over how generative AI services can be trained.

UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs, including The Temptations' "My Girl," to train its artificial intelligence system without permission. Udio's technology allows users to create original music from text prompts using AI. The specific financial terms of the settlement were not disclosed.

Under the new agreement, Udio will launch a platform next year trained exclusively on authorized and licensed music, allowing artists to participate and receive compensation. This marks Udio's first licensing deal with a major music label. UMG's CEO stated the company remains committed to supporting artists while embracing new technologies. Additionally, UMG announced a partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
State Farm's defense lawyers apologized after being caught submitting court filings containing artificial intelligence-generated fake legal cases, nonexistent quotes, and fabricated legal holdings in a lawsuit brought by Los Angeles homeowner Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga. The homeowner sued State Farm in July 2024 after a 2020 fire made her Carson home uninhabitable, followed by water damage during repairs. She claimed State Farm delayed approving repair work, leaving the house unfinished while she and her husband exhausted their savings, retirement accounts, and eventually lost their home to foreclosure.

Attorney Jacquelene Robinson acknowledged using an AI tool called Irys to help prepare the filings, which contained seven fake case citations across eight documents. Lead counsel Kenneth Katel accepted responsibility despite claiming he was unaware AI had been used. The error reflects a growing trend in the legal industry, with 41 percent of law firms now using generative AI tools. A Paris-based database has documented 1,922 legal hallucination cases worldwide, mostly in the United States. The case is scheduled for trial in October.

stories.Headline: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Extend Partnership in AI and Data
stories.Summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen their cooperation in artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technologies. The agreement was announced following a meeting between Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority President Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. The two nations plan to establish a comprehensive and long-term technology partnership.

During the discussion, Pakistan's minister outlined the country's national AI and data governance initiatives while reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to building a strong data ecosystem and growing its digital economy. Both countries intend to collaborate on emerging technologies and create a lasting framework for cooperation. The partnership reflects a broader regional focus on advancing artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, technology skills, and data-driven development.

stories.Headline: Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic Bring Free AI Bootcamp to Denver Teens
stories.Summary:
The Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic are offering a free artificial intelligence bootcamp to high school students in Denver this fall. The program is open to ninth through twelfth graders and will run over three consecutive Saturdays on October 31, November 7, and November 14. All costs including meals, transportation, and technology will be covered for participants at no charge. Applications close on September 30.

The bootcamp provides hands-on experience with AI tools and explores real-world applications across fields like healthcare, business, sports science, and career preparation. Students will work on a capstone project guided by industry mentors. This Denver bootcamp is one of more than 35 similar programs being hosted across the United States by various companies. Mark Cuban emphasized the importance of providing AI education to underserved students to prepare them for future educational and employment opportunities.

stories.Headline: Datametrex Plans to Focus on AI, Data Centre, and Patent Licensing
stories.Summary:
Datametrex AI Limited announced plans to wind down its healthcare operations to concentrate on artificial intelligence, data centre technology, and patent licensing. The company currently operates medical clinics in Edmonton, Calgary, and Vancouver, British Columbia, providing primary and emergency care services. Management intends to gradually reduce and eventually eliminate these healthcare operations while taking a measured approach based on operational, financial, contractual, and regulatory factors.

The strategic shift aims to simplify the company's structure, optimize resources, reduce regulatory compliance requirements, and improve financial performance. By refocusing on its core technology businesses, Datametrex expects to allocate capital and management attention toward long-term objectives while assessing opportunities to maximize value from healthcare assets during the transition. The company will provide additional announcements as the wind-down process progresses.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Headline: The 3 Best Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks for September
stories.Summary:
September typically presents challenges for stock market investors, as the month has historically produced more down months than any other for the S&P 500 and often results in negative returns over the long term. However, the article identifies three artificial intelligence stocks that offer compelling buying opportunities. Nvidia, Amazon, and Micron are recommended as top picks for September investment, with each company positioned to benefit from growing AI demand and infrastructure investment.

Nvidia continues to lead the AI sector, having delivered exceptional earnings with revenue growth of 106 percent year over year. The company's management team projected 70 percent revenue growth for the following fiscal year, significantly exceeding Wall Street expectations. Micron manufactures memory chips currently in short supply due to surging AI demand, with prices elevated and the shortage expected to persist until 2028. Amazon, through its cloud computing division AWS, is investing heavily in infrastructure and experiencing accelerating growth rates of 37 percent year over year in its second quarter, with AWS generating 60 percent of the company's operating income.

stories.Headline: Ghana: Ai Will Enhance, Not Replace Surveyors - Ghis President
stories.Summary:
Emmanuel K. Cobbold, president of the Ghana Institution of Surveyors, addressed members at the organization's 57th Founder's Day Anniversary Celebration in Accra. He encouraged surveyors to adopt artificial intelligence and emerging technologies rather than viewing them as threats to their profession. Cobbold emphasized that while AI can assist with measurements, data analysis, and interpretation, professional surveying still requires human judgment, local expertise, and ethical responsibility. He warned that surveyors who fail to adapt to technological changes risk becoming obsolete as the profession evolves.

The institution is working to help members upgrade their skills to meet changing technological demands while maintaining professional integrity standards. Sarah Esi Ziddah, the organization's chief executive officer, noted that surveyors have significantly contributed to Ghana's development, including providing geospatial data during a boundary dispute with Côte d'Ivoire and supporting construction of an infectious disease center. The event brought together current and former members to recognize contributions to the profession and strengthen professional connections among the organization's widely dispersed membership.

stories.Headline: Environmental News Network - AI Project Led by UH Aims to Protect Hawaiʻi's Coastal Freshwater
stories.Summary:
The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa is launching an artificial intelligence project to forecast threats to coastal freshwater supplies and ecosystems. Associate Professor Jonghyun Lee received a $500,000 grant from the National Science Foundation to lead the initiative, which is part of a broader three-year collaborative effort worth nearly $1 million involving the University of Texas at Austin. The project aims to develop AI applications in geoscience to better understand environmental challenges.

Rising ocean levels, intensified storms, saltwater infiltration of freshwater sources, and coastal ecosystem damage present growing dangers to communities throughout the region. These threats directly endanger drinking water availability, farming operations, infrastructure, and the economic wellbeing of millions of people who depend on coastal areas.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

India is hosting its first dedicated summit focused on artificial intelligence in marketing in September 2026. The AIM Summit will take place on September 17 in Bengaluru and September 18 in New Delhi, bringing together over 50 chief marketing officers from major brands including Paytm, KFC, Nestle, and Uniqlo. The event expects to attract more than 600 marketing professionals as attendees and delegates.

The summit aims to move beyond theoretical discussions about artificial intelligence and instead focus on practical implementation and real-world applications. The program will include an AI Lab for hands-on exploration of technology capabilities, an exhibition showcasing marketing solution providers, and an awards ceremony recognizing innovative organizations. Sessions will cover topics such as content creation, personalization, customer experience, marketing automation, and analytics. The summit is being organized with CXO Lanes, a community of over 500,000 executives across India.
